_what: THE PICTURE-PLANT MORGUE — known-bad delivered frames, kept as pictures.
LOOP-PROCESS §4 requires a plant: one deliberately wrong candidate seeded into the set, and
if the critic does not catch it the round is VOID and its findings are not read.
Every plant this project has built before now was GENERATED — plant_ashlar.py, plant_walls.py,
plant_family.py — a ruined family composed by the same composer from the same material. That
shape has failed four times in the recorded ledger, and each failure has the same root: the
plant is downstream of the engine, so an engine change can neutralise it silently.
wall round 9   VOID — plant missed. The plant was not in the picture.
wall round 10  VOID — plant missed. Since the cap pass the cell's base is a cap window and
the wall family's top tiles are never drawn, so a plant that ruined only the
wall tiles differed from the family in 0.54% of pixels, in 21 cells.
wall rounds 3, 6  VOID — the plant was culled for something the family shared.
A PICTURE CANNOT BE NEUTRALISED BY AN ENGINE CHANGE. These bytes are fixed. The defect in them
is fixed. The only way to stop a morgue entry carrying its defect is to delete the file, which
is a visible diff.
WHAT QUALIFIES FOR ENTRY. A frame Rafe personally culled at the device gate (§1's landing
gate), with his verbatim words and the commit whose build produced it. Not a frame an
instrument disliked; not a frame I thought was weak. The morgue is a record of human culls.
SURFACE TAGS ARE LOAD-BEARING. The deck draws a plant of the SAME surface as the round. A
floor plant in a wall round is caught for its magenta wall mocks — the critic flags the right
image for the wrong reason, and a control that greens for the wrong reason is not a control
(LOOP-PROCESS §4.2). run_frame_critic.sh refuses to build a deck if the surface has no entry.
KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than discovered later: the `wall` lane holds ONE entry. Wall rounds
therefore draw the same plant every time. That is safe against the seat, which is fresh each
round and cannot remember, and it is NOT safe against a builder who learns to compose around
one picture. Add wall entries as wall culls happen.

SURFACE IS A STRING OR A LIST, added for the combined round (2026-09-03). That round judges a whole room and the morgue was tagged when every round judged one surface at a time. Which entries can serve it was settled by READING THE PICTURES rather than the tags: the three floor culls each carry 3904 magenta pixels and would be caught for the debug colour instead of for their defect (§4.2); the two wall culls carry none and already have the real floor under them. Every entry now records that finding in `combined_eligibility`, so the next reader does not have to re-measure it.
AND THE `combined` LANE THEREFORE HOLDS TWO ENTRIES, which is the same known limit the wall lane is recorded with above and one entry better. Add combined entries as combined culls happen.

_why_this_is_a_plant_and_not_a_null: §13.6 — a candidate never contributes to its own acceptance bar — and RULED SATISFIED
(Rafe, 2026-09-07) on a distinction worth keeping straight:
A NULL is the same build with one lever switched off. It is a CONTROL: it says what the
lever contributed. It is not a plant, because nobody ever culled it.
THIS is a SUPERSEDED BUILD that two independent eyes culled on the axis now under test.
It earned its place in the morgue the way every other entry did — by being rejected —
and it is here because it is WRONG ON TONE, which is the question round 5 asks.
The hazard §13.6 guards against is choosing a plant that flatters the build. This one does
the opposite: it is the build's own immediate predecessor, identical in scene, station,
geometry and rig, differing ONLY on the axis being judged. A seat that cannot separate
them has told us something real about the shoulder, not about the deck.
entries.combined_eligibility: ELIGIBLE, and it is the first entry captured AS a combined frame. The three FLOOR culls are ineligible for carrying 3904 debug-magenta pixels; this one carries none.

entries.defect: THE LANE STOPS BEING THE SAME MASONRY. At 1.9 the specular washes the stones inside the trodden channel until the path reads as re-laid rather than worn. Measured on this frame with measure_lane_window.py: on-lane masonry 0.1003 — 0.70x §13.8's 0.1440 floor, so the joints and dressing inside the lane fall BELOW what a viewer can resolve — and identity_ratio 0.943, i.e. THE LANE IS LESS LEGIBLE THAN ITS OWN FLANK. That inversion is the defect stated as a number: wear is modulating the same stones everywhere except where it is strongest, and there it replaces them. The shipped build reads 0.1513 (1.05x) and identity 1.150 on the same measure.
entries.seeded: RULED (Rafe, 2026-09-08): 'Seed a second tonal plant: the lane-gain-1.9 replaced tiles build (Rafe's cull quoted; on-lane identity < flank measured). Two tonal plants; seats draw one at random.' It exists because the combined/tonal set had exactly ONE member, so every seat of a panel drew the same plant and their catches were CORRELATED — the panel multiplied rank samples but not the plant's evidence.

axis_retagged.by: builder, under LOOP-PROCESS §1.1.5.2 (plant axis mismatch is engineering)
axis_retagged.why: SEEDED AS TONAL BY RULING (Rafe, 2026-09-08) and re-tagged on the evidence of its own outings. The CULL'S PERCEPT is material identity — 'it looks like all the tiles on the walked path have been replaced' — not tone. Its MECHANISM is specular, which is what I tagged it on, and §1.2.1 is explicit that a plant controls on the axis its cull was made on rather than the axis of whatever produced it. The morgue's own precedent settles it: washed-slab-lane.png carries the same percept — washed slabs on the walked path — and is tagged VALUE.
axis_retagged.operational_evidence: caught 3 of 5 across this lane, against blown-highlight's 7 of 7, and it voided two of four rounds on polish-abc-install. ⚠ n=5 is thin — the 95% interval on 3/5 spans roughly 15-95% — so the catch rate is SUGGESTIVE and the AXIS ARGUMENT is what decides this, not the count.
axis_retagged.cost_restored: the combined/tonal set returns to one member, so every seat of a tonal panel draws the same plant and their catches are correlated again. That is the limitation this entry was seeded to remove and it is NOT solved; a genuinely tonal second cull is still wanted.
axis_retagged.kept: nothing is deleted — the entry, its bytes, its quote and its provenance all stand.

The cap was later OVERTURNED at the human gate (Rafe, 2026-09-09) — 'warmest never brightest' meant NEVER BLOWN, not darker than the ground — and this frame is the blown end that both the original ruling and the overturn agree is wrong.
_the_cull_is_the_lighting_not_the_sprite: RULED (Rafe, 2026-09-11), and it decides how this entry must be read:
'the cull was the lighting blowing out its subject, not the hero's design.'
The figure here is the ORYX PLACEHOLDER. It is not Sasha, it is not being worked, and
a seat flagging its ART rather than its EXPOSURE has caught this frame for the wrong
reason — which LOOP-PROCESS §4.2 says is not a control at all. What makes it a plant is
that the lamp destroys whatever is standing there.
_why_this_is_admissible_when_a_null_norm: ⚠ THIS FILE IS THE NULL ARM OF #183'S OWN SWEEP, and `blown-highlight.png`'s entry
states the general law against exactly that: 'A NULL is the same build with one lever
switched off ... It is not a plant, because nobody ever culled it.'
The reason that law gives is the reason it does not bite here. THIS STATE WAS CULLED:
Rafe walked it on 2026-09-06 and #183 exists because of it. The null is not a
manufactured picture nobody judged — it is the faithful capture of a shipped state that
was judged and rejected, with the lever that fixed it not yet written.
THE ALTERNATIVES WERE CHECKED AND REJECTED, by measurement rather than by preference:
* rerat_r1.png, the actual walked frame, IS ALREADY IN THIS MORGUE — it is
blown-highlight.png, byte for byte. Planting it twice under two labels would put the
same picture in two seats' decks and call it decorrelation.
* swB_e1.6.png is the same build in the probe room, with an identical 784-pixel figure
clip — but it differs from the planted frame by only 1.61% of pixels. Two plants
that look the same defeat the thing the second plant is for.
* h_null differs from the planted frame by 10.55%, in the same scene, at the ratified
rig, with the real wall and cap families laid and zero magenta.
entries.combined_eligibility: ELIGIBLE. Same scene as the deck (tier1_combined_review), ratified rig (energy 1.6 / radius 6.0 / ambient 1.5), real wall and cap families, ZERO magenta pixels. It predates the tier-two props, as does the approved reference and the existing tonal plant.

_the_morgue_had_no_dark_side: THIS IS THE FIRST DARK-SIDE PLANT. Every tonal entry before it fails BRIGHT — the lamp
clipping, the highlight blowing. A panel whose only tonal controls are blown frames
teaches a seat one direction of the axis, and a build that errs the other way meets a
judge that has never been asked about it.
It is also the oldest cull in the morgue and the only one from a DEVICE GATE rather
than a walk — the round where every instrument was green and the phone still said no.
entries.combined_eligibility: ELIGIBLE. ZERO magenta: it was captured with the real floor, wall and binding families laid. ⚠ It is at the PRE-RE-RATIFICATION rig (radius 5.0 / ambient 0.70), because that is the rig it was culled at — the crush is partly what the re-ratification fixed. That is the defect, not a confound: a seat is being asked which frame is tonally wrong, and this one is, for the reason recorded.
